useCase.name: Reach everyone at once with an urgent message written by the sender, across every channel

intent.name: emergency.permission.set
intent.summary: Set who holds the right to send an emergency notice. Super Admin only, one step.
routesHere: give the Principal the emergency send permission

routesHere.text: Principal ko emergency paighaam bhejne ka ikhtiyar de do
routesHere.gloss: give the Principal the right to send an emergency message

routesHere.text: School Admin se ye ikhtiyar wapas le lo
routesHere.gloss: take this right away from the School Admin

routesHere.text: emergency bhejne ka haq kaun rakhta hai, tay karo
routesHere.gloss: set who holds the right to send an emergency

request.text: manzoori ka marhala bhi rakh do
request.gloss: add an approval step as well

routesElsewhere.note: There is no approval step. An emergency message that waits for a second person is a message that arrives late, and the control is the permission rather than the approval (BR-9, E5).

steps.note: One step. It is a permission, not a fixed role, so the school decides who holds it rather than the software deciding (BR-1).

plan.atomicity: One write: the holders and the audit entry together or not at all. Whoever holds it can send to everybody, on every channel, with no approval — so the permission is the whole control (BR-9). Either the School Admin or the Principal can hold it, and both are named because in a real emergency whichever of them is at the school sends it (BR-2).

operations.name: emergency.permission.set
operations.idempotencyKey: branch_id, since a branch carries one set of holders
operations.purpose: Set which users hold the emergency send permission.

parameters.name: holders
parameters.notes: The users who hold the right (BR-1). The complete list, not an addition — a name absent from it loses the permission. Either the School Admin or the Principal can hold it, and a permission attached to only one is a permission that is absent half the time (BR-2).

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

fields.name: holders
fields.description: Who holds it now, by name and role.

fields.name: added
fields.description: Users who did not hold it before.

fields.name: removed
fields.description: Users who held it and now do not.

fields.name: holder_count
fields.description: How many. A permission held by nobody present is a permission that is absent when it is needed (BR-2).

fields.name: set_by
fields.description: The Super Admin (BR-1).

errors.meaning: A non-Super Admin attempted to set the permission.
errors.note: The right is granted by the Super Admin (BR-1).

errors.meaning: The change would leave nobody holding it.
errors.note: Nobody could then send an emergency notice at all.

planningRules.rule: Never add or remove a holder the actor did not name. The list is complete rather than incremental, and a name dropped in passing is somebody who cannot send when the school is on fire.

Report who holds it after the change, by name and role. Both the School Admin and the Principal are named in the rule because whichever of them is at the school sends it (BR-2), and a list of one is a permission absent half the time.
Never propose an approval step. There is none by design — an emergency message that waits for a second person arrives late, and the permission is the control (BR-9, E5).
Report where a holder is leaving the school. A permission held by somebody who has exited is a permission nobody can use (A6).

reversal.statement: The permission is set again rather than withdrawn, and every change is recorded with who made it.

request.text: Principal ko bhi ye ikhtiyar de do
request.gloss: give the Principal this right as well

resolvedPlans.context: Super Admin, with the School Admin currently holding it.

inputs.holders: the complete list the Super Admin named — the School Admin and the Principal

steps.note: The list is complete, not an addition to what was there (PR-1).

resolvedPlans.outcome: Set. Report both holders by name (PR-2) — whichever of them is at the school can send, which is why the rule names both rather than picking one.

resolvedPlans.context: Super Admin, on a permission currently held by the School Admin alone.

inputs.holders: $request.holders — the complete list, which the actor has not stated

steps.note: No plan is emitted until the full list is confirmed (PR-1).

resolvedPlans.outcome: Nothing is set. Report who holds it now and confirm the complete list — the call replaces it, so sending the Principal alone would take the right away from the School Admin and leave them unable to send in an emergency.

request.text: emergency bhejne se pehle Principal ki manzoori zaroori kar do
request.gloss: require the Principal's approval before an emergency is sent

steps.note: No approval step can be planned — there is none (PR-3).

resolvedPlans.outcome: Report that the design has no approval step and cannot be given one here: a message that waits for a second person arrives late, and the control is who holds the permission. If the Principal should be the one deciding, the answer is to hold the permission themselves — which is what setting the holders does.

intent.name: emergency.notice.send
intent.summary: Write an urgent message and send it to everybody, on every channel, at once. One step, no approval, and it cannot be recalled.
routesHere: send an emergency notice — the school is closing at noon

routesHere.text: emergency paighaam bhej do — school aaj dopahar band ho raha hai
routesHere.gloss: send an emergency notice — the school is closing at noon today

routesHere.text: foran sab ko itla kar do
zaroori notice sab walidain aur staff ko bhejo
routesHere.gloss: send an urgent notice to all parents and staff

routesHere: send this district notice to everyone with the order attached

routesElsewhere.note: It goes to everyone. Nobody is selected, because selecting takes time and an emergency is the case where the school would rather over-send (BR-5, E6). Whether it can be limited to one class or campus is an open question in this use case.
There is no template step, because the wording of an emergency is the sender's and a template would be a delay and a wrong wording at once (BR-3).

request.text: bhejne ke baad wapas le lo

routesElsewhere.note: An emergency notice cannot be recalled once sent. A correction is a second notice, and both stay on the record (BR-10, E7).

request.text: baad mein bhejne ke liye schedule kar do

routesElsewhere.note: Nothing about the notice is templated, scheduled or queued behind ordinary traffic. It goes ahead of every other message waiting to be sent (BR-11).

steps.note: One step, and it reaches every parent, every student, every teacher and every member of staff, across every available channel at once (BR-5, BR-6). There is no approval and no queue — it goes ahead of every other message waiting to be sent (BR-9, BR-11).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. An empty message is not sent; no channel configured at all sends nothing and is reported rather than appearing to succeed.
plan.atomicity: One write, and it is irreversible: the notice, the send across every channel, and the log of the sender, the time, the message and any attachment (BR-8). **It cannot be recalled** — a correction is a second notice and both stay on the record (BR-10). A channel without balance is skipped and the shortfall is reported at once (E4); a channel that cannot carry the attachment sends the message anyway and the rest are told where to find it (E8).

operations.name: emergency.notice.send
operations.idempotencyKey: message + sender + minute, so a double press does not send every family two emergency notices
operations.purpose: Send an emergency notice to everybody across every channel.

parameters.name: message
parameters.notes: 10 to 1000 characters, written by the sender (BR-3, E2). There is no template step — the wording of an emergency is theirs, and a message a planner drafted is the school telling every family something nobody chose to say.

parameters.name: attachment_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No uploaded file matches. The document is attached on the screen first.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the files uploaded for this notice.

parameters.notes: A document sent with the message where one is needed — a district notice, a road closure order, a health advisory (BR-4). Attached on the screen and named here.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

returns.description: The send and what it reached.

fields.name: notice_id
fields.description: The notice.

fields.name: sender
fields.description: Whoever holds the permission, recorded by name (BR-8).

fields.name: sent_at
fields.description: When.

fields.name: recipients
fields.description: Everybody — every parent, student, teacher and member of staff. Not chosen (BR-5).

fields.name: channels_used
fields.description: Every available channel at once rather than one after another (BR-6).

fields.name: delivered
fields.description: How many were delivered, per channel (BR-7).

fields.name: failed
fields.description: Recipients not reached after retries, listed by name so the school knows who to telephone (BR-7).

fields.name: delivery_unknown
fields.description: Where a provider's delivery reporting is unavailable, delivery reads unknown rather than delivered (E9).

fields.name: channels_without_balance
fields.description: Channels skipped for want of balance, reported at once (E4).

fields.name: attachment_not_carried
fields.description: Channels that could not carry the attachment. The message still went, and the rest are told where to find it (E8).

fields.name: unreachable_contacts
fields.description: Numbers the directory already knew could not be reached (UC-14-02 BR-7).

errors.meaning: The acting user does not hold the emergency send permission.
errors.note: The right is granted by the Super Admin (BR-1).

errors.meaning: No channel is configured at all.
errors.note: Reported rather than appearing to succeed.

errors.meaning: There is no messaging balance on some channels.
errors.written: The notice is sent on the channels that have balance.
errors.note: The shortfall is reported at once, since the missing channel may be the one a family actually reads.

errors.meaning: The attachment is too large for a channel.
errors.written: The message goes on every channel.
errors.notWritten: The attachment goes only on those that can carry it.
errors.note: The rest are told where to find it.

planningRules.rule: Never write or reword the message. The wording of an emergency is the sender's (BR-3), and a message a planner drafted is the school telling every family in it something nobody decided to say.

Never narrow the recipients. It goes to everyone, because selecting takes time and an emergency is the case where the school would rather over-send (BR-5, E6) — and whether it can be limited at all is an open question here.
Say plainly that it cannot be recalled before it goes. A correction is a second notice and both stay on the record (BR-10, E7) — this is the message a school is asked about afterwards.
Report the failed recipients by name. A recipient the message did not reach is somebody the school now has to telephone, and a count does not tell anybody who (BR-7).
Report a channel skipped for want of balance at once. The missing channel may be the one a particular family actually reads, and the send will otherwise look like a success (E4).
Report delivery as unknown where a provider cannot say. It is not the same as delivered, and treating it as such is how a family is assumed to have been told (E9).
Never suggest an approval, a template, a schedule or a queue. None exists by design, and each would be a delay in the one message where a delay is the harm (BR-9, BR-11).

reversal.statement: There is no recall. A correction is a second notice, and both stay on the record (BR-10, E7). The controller must not attempt a compensating call — every family has already been messaged.

request.text: emergency paighaam bhej do — school aaj dopahar band ho raha hai
request.gloss: send an emergency notice — the school is closing at noon today

resolvedPlans.context: Principal, Johar Town branch, holding the permission, message written.
resolvedPlans.outcome: Say before sending that it goes to every parent, student and member of staff on every channel and cannot be recalled (PR-3). After: report delivered per channel, the failures by name so the office can telephone them (PR-4), and any channel skipped for want of balance (PR-5).

request.text: foran sab ko itla kar do ke school band hai, paighaam tum likh do
request.gloss: tell everybody at once that the school is closed — you write the message

resolvedPlans.context: School Admin, Johar Town branch, holding the permission.

steps.note: No plan is emitted. The wording is the sender's (PR-1).

resolvedPlans.outcome: Nothing is sent. Ask for the message in their own words — it reaches every family in the school in one act, it cannot be recalled, and it is the message the school is asked about afterwards. Drafting it here would put words the Principal never chose in front of every parent.

request.text: sirf class 5 ke walidain ko emergency bhejo
request.gloss: send the emergency to class 5 parents only

steps.note: The capability sends to everyone. There is no recipient parameter to narrow (PR-2).

resolvedPlans.outcome: Report before sending that an emergency notice goes to everybody — there is no way to limit it here, and whether it should be limitable to a class or a campus is an open question this use case raises and does not answer. If only class 5 should be told, an ordinary class message is the route; if it is genuinely an emergency, it goes to all.

intent.name: emergency.notice.delivery.read
intent.summary: Read who an emergency notice reached and who it did not. One step, reads only, and the failures come back by name.
routesHere: who did not get the emergency notice?

routesHere.text: emergency paighaam kis kis tak nahi pahuncha
routesHere.gloss: who did not receive the emergency notice

routesHere.text: kitne log reh gaye, naam bata do
routesHere.gloss: how many were missed — give me the names

routesElsewhere.note: A resend is a second notice, and both stay on the record (BR-10).

request.text: jo reh gaye un ko phone kar do
request.gloss: telephone the ones who were missed

routesElsewhere.note: The list exists so the school knows who to telephone (BR-7). The telephoning is done by people.

steps.note: One step, and it reads only. Delivery is monitored and failures are retried; a recipient the message did not reach is listed by name, so the school knows who to telephone (BR-7).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. There is nothing to undo — nothing was written.
plan.atomicity: No write. It answers the question the school asks in the hour after an emergency: who has not been told. A delivery a provider cannot confirm reads unknown rather than delivered (E9), because assuming somebody was told is how a family is left out of an evacuation.

operations.name: emergency.notice.delivery.read
operations.purpose: Read the delivery state of an emergency notice.

parameters.name: notice_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No emergency notice matches within the actor's scope.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the notices with their time, sender and opening words.

parameters.notes: The notice, resolved from when it was sent or what it said.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

fields.name: notice_id
fields.description: The notice.

fields.name: sent_at
fields.description: When it went.

fields.name: sender
fields.description: Who sent it (BR-8).

fields.name: delivered
fields.description: Per channel, how many were delivered (BR-7).

fields.name: failed
fields.description: Each recipient not reached after retries, by name and number, so the school knows who to telephone (BR-7).

fields.name: delivery_unknown
fields.description: Recipients whose provider could not report. Unknown is not delivered (E9).

fields.name: never_reachable
fields.description: Recipients whose numbers the directory already knew could not be reached (UC-14-02 BR-7).

fields.name: no_contact_at_all
fields.description: People with no contact number, who were never in the send at all (UC-14-02 E8).

fields.name: retries_remaining
fields.description: Whether retries are still running. How many before a delivery is abandoned is not decided.

errors.meaning: The notice is outside the actor's scope.

planningRules.rule: Report the failures by name and number, never as a count. The list exists so somebody can pick up a telephone (BR-7), and a total tells them nothing about whom to call.

Report unknown delivery separately from delivered. Where a provider cannot confirm, the notice still sent but nobody knows it arrived (E9) — counting it as delivered is how a family is assumed to have been told.

Report the people who were never in the send. Somebody with no contact number at all does not appear as a failure, because they were never a recipient (UC-14-02 E8) — they are the ones nothing ever fails loudly for.
Say whether retries are still running. How many before a delivery is abandoned is not decided anywhere in this use case, so a failure list read too early is not final.
Never resend as part of reading. A resend is a second notice to everybody, and both stay on the record (BR-10).

reversal.statement: Nothing was written, so there is nothing to reverse.

request.text: emergency paighaam kis kis tak nahi pahuncha
request.gloss: who did not receive the emergency notice

resolvedPlans.context: Principal, Johar Town branch, minutes after the send.
resolvedPlans.outcome: Report the failures by name and number so the office can start telephoning (PR-1), the deliveries the providers could not confirm as unknown rather than delivered (PR-2), and the people who were never in the send at all because no number is held for them (PR-3). Say whether retries are still running (PR-4).

request.text: bas ye bata do kitne deliver hue
request.gloss: just tell me how many were delivered

resolvedPlans.outcome: Give the number, then give the names behind the failures anyway (PR-1). In an emergency the useful figure is not how many were reached but which families were not — the count is what makes a send look successful when eleven households have heard nothing.

request.text: jo reh gaye un ko dobara bhej do
request.gloss: resend to the ones who were missed

steps.note: The read only. No resend is chained (PR-5).

resolvedPlans.outcome: The failures come back by name. Report that there is no targeted resend — an emergency notice goes to everybody, so sending again reaches every family a second time, and both notices stay on the record. For eleven households, telephoning is what the list is for.
